primary_goals: Stay available for selection every week through the second half of the season
Hold my strength and sprint speed from now to the end of the season
secondary_goals: Improve repeated-sprint ability late in matches
maintenance_goals: Maintain the squat and hamstring strength I have
inseason_footballer.equipment: Full club gym: barbells, dumbbells, racks, Nordic bench, sled, cable machines.
inseason_footballer.current_numbers:
Back Squat: 150 kg x 1
Trap Bar Deadlift: 200 kg x 3
Nordic hamstring: 3 controlled reps each side
30 m sprint: 4.05 s
Currently 5 football sessions plus a match most weeks
inseason_footballer.injuries: Right hamstring: two grade-1 biceps femoris strains in the last 18 months, most recently 4 months ago. Currently symptom-free and fully training, but it tightens in the last 15 minutes of matches.

pain.description: No current pain; occasional right hamstring tightness late in matches
pain.tolerated_movements: All football work, sprinting, squatting and hinging are tolerated. Heavy eccentric hamstring work the day before a match is not.

inseason_footballer.notes: This is an in-season block, not a pre-season one. There is a competitive match most Saturdays and the season runs well past this block, so there is no single event to peak for and no taper: the athlete has to be ready every single week. Matchday is Saturday. Two 45-minute gym sessions on Tuesday and Thursday, both after football. Gym work exists to keep him available and fast, never to make him sore for a match. Hamstring reinjury is the thing that would end his season.

primary_goals: Return to competitive masters rowing and race a 2 km erg again
secondary_goals: Rebuild lower-body and trunk strength safely
maintenance_goals: Keep the upper-body and aerobic base I still have
masters_return.equipment: Full gym with rowing ergometer, barbells, dumbbells, cables, and a leg press.
masters_return.current_numbers:
2 km erg: 8:58 nine months ago, not tested since
Goblet squat: 24 kg x 8 comfortable
Deadlift: not attempted since the injury
Currently 2 easy erg sessions a week, 20-30 min each
masters_return.injuries: L4/L5 disc herniation nine months ago with right-leg symptoms. Discharged from physiotherapy six weeks ago and cleared for graded loading. No leg symptoms for three months. Loaded lumbar flexion under fatigue is the movement that reproduced symptoms.

pain.description: Occasional low-back stiffness in the morning and after long sitting
pain.tolerated_movements: Erg at low rate, goblet squats, split squats, cable work, carries and hip thrusts are all comfortable. Repeated loaded spinal flexion under fatigue is not, and was what caused the original injury.

mobility.limitation: Guarded lumbar flexion; hip flexion range is fine

masters_return.notes: Post-menopausal, so bone loading matters and recovery is genuinely slower than it was. Returning after nine months away, discharged from physio and cleared for graded loading, but has not deadlifted since the injury and is nervous about it. Wants to race masters again rather than just be pain-free. The 2 km erg is the goal, but rowing is the exact movement that loads the injured tissue, so the return has to be built rather than assumed. Do not prescribe rehabilitation or treat this as a medical case: she is discharged and cleared. Train her.
